note: The improver's answers to the owner's dashboard notes (agents/improver.md section 0b). Imported by the ingest workflow, which marks each note addressed and shows the answer on the dashboard.

acks.note: Started A/B money-travels-not-pops on half the Shorts: money now flies on an arc between the things it connects (customer to restaurant to McDonald's) and things fly in and land instead of popping; reference-based research on animation continues in research's reports.

Pop-and-shake replaced on half the Shorts (A/B money-travels-not-pops): things fly in or grow out of the thing before them and land with a squash, shake is a hop, and money travels with its figure riding on it; checked on this video's own timeline.
Same fix as the McDonald's note: on the A/B's on-half, every beat where money changes hands shows notes travelling between the two things, so the middle of the video always has something moving.

Built a livelier cinematic bed (major-first chords, soft kick and shaker from the first bar, snare after the hook) behind flag cinematic-bed-gets-a-pulse; it starts as an A/B as soon as an experiment slot frees (5 of 5 running, next frees in about a day). Cinematic is our best genre by % viewed (69.6%, n=6), so it stays and gets energy.

Your pattern ('You think McDonald's makes its money from burgers? It doesn't.') is the next hook experiment (hook-you-think-x-youre-wrong); it starts the night hook-voice-matches-frame gets its verdict, about one more Short, so two hook tests don't blur each other.

'Let me show you why' gives the viewer nothing to guess; the next hook experiment (hook-you-think-x-youre-wrong: put the belief to the viewer and deny it, never the answer) starts once the current hook test ends in about a day.

Read as taste: how-famous-companies-make-money stories with a clear money route; research added three more (gym, Costco, Starbucks) to the feed, and the new travelling-money animation is built for exactly this story.

Rebuilt after a frame-by-frame study of The Curious Plot: a question in the viewer's voice every 12 s, answers early then deeper, real names with sourced facts, every figure built from units with the sum on screen, a named term per step, an ending that asks the viewer something; checked by code (generator/story.py). Shown to you as the v-remake-salary demo.

The new board scene: questions in a room, every answer a full-frame labelled card (documents with real data, sums, chips, charts, things that turn into and feed each other), a new picture every sentence, every clause animated (90%+ gate), readable on mute (QA check). Approved on the fourth demo take.
Stale. Its 9 hedging words and a 'Picture...' opener now fail the number check, so a script like it can't ship again; the topic is kept and remade as v-remake-car.
Stale. The new storytelling and presentation rules (one concrete story, open questions, the camera following the action) apply to every Short from the next run.
Things in board and build beats no longer wait on screen: anything nothing acts on until 0.6 s into a beat now flies in just before the word that names it, then animates.

New render check: a board video fails when more than 65% of its actions only mark something already there (this Short had 71%: glows, stamps, bubbles), so writers must add things that enter, swap, flow, multiply or a panel.
The 'Data:' source line now prints once a video, on the first beat that says a sourced figure; a video's own beats that print it everywhere fail the own-code check.
Writer rule: a real company is shown by its name (a name card or a label on its product), never a pun object like fruit for Apple; real logos can't be used (no downloaded images, trademarks).
Writer rule: the first time a real person is named they get one short clause that makes them matter; a rank or amount in it must be a sourced fact, otherwise words.

Real faces and logos would need downloaded images, which the hard rules forbid (no downloaded or copyrighted assets), and bring likeness and trademark risk; companies now show by name instead. Only you can change that rule (see Notifications).
Taken as taste: v-20261103-02's board mix (more things entering and growing, fewer marks) is the bar the new 65% mark cap is set against.

Found it: on a card the person card and the two documents hid every prop for 12 s; now a Short's card keeps its things standing under one person card or short document (stills: cash case, shares and tax envelope back at 5-15 s), and the checklist forbids card beats without things.

Added a shared 'city' prop (a skyline of towers with lit windows, roofs and a crane, built up to k) so a city is never a tilted slab again, plus a checklist rule that places read as places; the disclaimer is now a small line at the very bottom of the frame at the minimum text size (commit 6226210).

Long videos now play at tempo 1.25 (~180 words a minute, was 1.5 / ~215); the long writer guide asks for 3-5 things per beat with an action on every clause (yours had 1.9), and a figure the sum already shows no longer slams in behind it (the QA-found overlap at 95 s and 285 s).

You're right: since 31 Oct every Short is about a named billionaire or company, while the 1K week mixed in the viewer's own money ('Your $20,000 savings' 1,161, 'Your Dhanteras necklace' 1,133); half of new Shorts now tell a big-money format through the viewer's own money, measured on 48 h views (experiment you-in-the-core-story).

A round million or billion now shows in words everywhere (titles, descriptions, on screen): '$10 billion', '$1 million', not '$10,000,000,000'; the number check rejects a title or description with 7+ digits, so it can't come back.

That Short (27 s) was in the variant system's 20-27 s length test, and so far the data favours it: 20-27 s Shorts have a median of 908 views at 48 h vs 133 for 28-35 s (n 5 vs 9). Lengths are owner-only (config/arms.json); if you still want 30 s at least, the steps are on the Notifications page.

Noted as your taste: that Short was a 'pick-one' shape with things that turn into each other (the bonus becoming a paycheck); pick-one is a trial shape and needs one more Short at the median to become a regular.
